fields.Description: This page from the International Cheese Federation provides a compilation of recent articles and updates, covering diverse topics such as member spotlights, industry news, advocacy efforts, educational content, upcoming events, and certification information. It also offers general organizational details, archives, categories, and resources for the global cheese community.

New member spotlight: a Jura affineur joins us 

 

Henri Dubois of Fromagerie Saint-Rémille joined the federation last month. He runs a maturation room in the Jura, he flips wheels by hand, and he has opinions about airflow. 


Continue Reading

Industry News 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Two markets, one cheese case 

 

Commodity cheese is drowning in surplus while our artisan members can’t make enough to fill orders. Both things are true at once, and the gap is where our members live. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



1 


 


Feb 



 


 

 

Advocacy 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The cheese nobody can move 

 

Cold-storage warehouses are holding more cheese than they ever have, exports are down, and farmgate milk prices are stuck. Here is what the federation is asking policymakers to do about it. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



30 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Education 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Listeria and the small cave: what environmental monitoring actually looks like 

 

Environmental monitoring sounds like a big-plant word, but it scales down fine. A look at what our Listeria Control course actually asks small creameries to do. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



28 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Industry News 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Reading the market without the data 

 

With federal statistics only now catching back up after a five-week lapse, members are pricing January without the usual numbers. Here’s what we do know. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



25 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Building the swab map at Quincewick Creamery 

 

Quality manager Aisha Bell walked us through her environmental monitoring program at Quincewick Creamery, sharing practical lessons on winter zone mapping, drain swabs, and sanitation hurdles for craft facilities. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



23 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Education 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Winter milk, calcium balance, and the make sheet 

 

When dairy herds transition to winter rations, shifts in fat-to-protein ratios and soluble calcium can destabilize curd formation. Here is how craft creameries adjust make sheets and vat timing for cold-weather milk. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



21 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Advocacy 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Raw milk, aged curds, and the line at the state border 

 

As state legislative sessions convene across the country, new bills on farmstead dairy sales are landing on committee dockets while artisan cheesemakers navigate federal sixty-day aging rules and interstate distribution limits. 


Continue Reading 



 
 

 
 



18 


 


Jan 



 


 

 

Events 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Two workshops in February, and a July date 

 

The Events Committee has the winter calendar out: packaging in Tandil on 18 February, food safety in Lancaster on 27 February, and the annual conference in Madison in July. 


Continue Reading

Jan 



 


 

 

Certification 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Credentials expire on their own schedule 

 

January is when the certificate surfaces in a drawer and nobody remembers the date on it. Here is how long each of our seven credentials runs, and which ones to check first.
